chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: The 1947 Cavalcade of Jazz program page on Spikes
summary: Willard reads a profile claiming Spikes organized a band in 1921, sent for Lionel Hampton, and led the first Black band recorded for Warner Brothers' sound film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you about this program here for the Cavalcade of Jazz, which was an annual event that Leon Heflin...
I told you that Leon Heflin...Heflin...uh, put that...
Right. I used to go to these--a little bit later than this but this is a 1947 program, and there's a whole page in here on you under "Platter Makers."
Yeah, I read that. I got that. Yeah.
Yeah, this is it. You loaned me this, and it says, "Reb Spikes, who started with the organizing of a band in 1921 and who sent for Lionel Hampton to come to the coast and who had Kid Ory and
Les Hite, now operates Music Town, the entire second floor at the corner of Normandie and Jefferson...
"In 1921 the band played over KFI with Kid Ory when they were still using earphones."
And, "They were the first Negro band to play for records..."
"...which were used by Warner Brothers to produce sound with motion pictures called Vitaphone."
